user_confirmed.regime_A: Electricity sales/supply and charging can compete freely; no supply guarantee
user_confirmed.regime_B: Parallel baseline with a supply-priority constraint
user_confirmed.objective: Maximise the scheme's net profit/net benefit; difference from the no-new-equipment scheme is a reported metric rather than a necessary objective transformation
user_confirmed.research_condition: Assume complete and coherent research interfaces for trading, batteries, electrolysers/hydrogen and financial parameters

assistant_assessment: A shared model with two policy regimes is structurally clear and aligned with the open-ended project brief. Research fills parameters and selected mechanisms; operational semantics must still be explicit rather than inferred from data availability.

proposed_executable_priority_definition.G_t: Fixed daily available energy from the given total generation plus the specified additional wind profile
proposed_executable_priority_definition.D_t: Given constructed-system demand, used as the sales/absorption limit in the working system convention
proposed_executable_priority_definition.q_t: Direct sale from current given generation; distinct from battery discharge sales
proposed_executable_priority_definition.regime_A: q_t chosen jointly with charging, hydrogen production, discharge and curtailment
proposed_executable_priority_definition.regime_B: q_t = min(G_t,D_t); only remaining current generation is available for charging/hydrogen/curtailment
proposed_executable_priority_definition.remaining_deficit: No automatic requirement to exhaust stored energy or buy power to fill residual demand; these stronger duties would require a separate explicit rule
proposed_executable_priority_definition.negative_prices: Supply priority still applies in B even if its sale cash flow is negative

common_accounting: Same data, technology candidates, financial horizon, prices, cost boundaries and starting/terminal inventories in A and B
No-new-equipment comparator evaluated under the matching policy regime
Choose a precise profit basis consistent with the time horizon: cumulative net cash benefit, discounted net benefit or annual-equivalent net benefit; avoid treating mismatched periods as comparable
Include relevant direct electricity sales, battery discharge sales, H2 sales, new investment and affected operating/purchase/replacement costs
Fixed existing sunk capital and unchanged existing costs may cancel in incremental comparisons
validation_implication: If B only adds constraints to A with identical variables, inputs and accounting, optimised absolute net profit in A cannot be below B. Regime-specific incremental profits need not have the same ordering because their no-investment comparators can differ.
implementation_conventions_to_document: Investment timing and fixed capacity over each evaluation run
Daily power/energy conversion, state continuity across missing dates, initial/terminal stock rules
Tier1 perfect-information operations versus separate held-out capacity and causal-operation evaluations
